Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`). Admin portal exists at `/admin/*`, nav config in `lib/admin-groups.ts` (an `AdminGroup[]`/`AdminEntry[]` structure — read a few existing groups before adding a new one, e.g. the `revenue` group which already has Billing/Catalog/Promotions entries).

## The ask

The owner wants to start treating Nxeon like a real business: a genuine accounting/finance section in the admin portal — expense tracking, and money tracking generally (revenue vs. costs, not just the existing customer-billing views). This is a foundational v1, not the final word — build something real and usable, use good judgment on scope, but don't try to build a full general-ledger accounting system in one pass.

## What already exists — don't duplicate, integrate with it

Real revenue data already lives in the DB and should be surfaced, not re-entered:
- `Invoice` model — customer invoices, `status`, `amountCents`.
- `WalletTransaction` — wallet credits/debits (includes admin adjustments, referral payouts, etc. — read `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts` and `lib/actions-affiliate.ts` for how these get created).
- `User.balanceCents` — current wallet balances.
- Stripe is the actual payment processor (`lib/stripe.ts`) — real charges/fees exist there too, though pulling live Stripe fee data may be more than v1 needs; note it as a possible future data source rather than building Stripe API integration now unless it's straightforward.

Real cost data that already exists and should be pulled in as automatic expense line items, not manually re-entered:
- The admin "Dedicated IP pool" page (`lib/dedicated-ip.ts`, look for the page under `app/admin/...` via `lib/admin-groups.ts`'s `fleet` group) already computes a real monthly OVH cost figure (currently ~$11.95/mo across several $2.39-3.19/IP additional IPs) — pull this in as a real recurring expense line, don't ask the owner to type it in by hand.
- If you can find where the platform tracks its own OVH dedicated server rental cost, or any other already-known recurring platform cost (check `lib/settings.ts` / `Setting` table for anything like a base infrastructure cost setting), surface that too. If nothing like that exists, that's fine — leave a clearly-labeled manual entry for it rather than guessing a number.

## What to build

1. **Schema** — an `Expense` model: id, description, `amountCents`, category (a sensible enum — e.g. `INFRASTRUCTURE`, `SOFTWARE`, `PAYMENT_PROCESSING`, `MARKETING`, `LEGAL`, `OTHER` — use your judgment on a reasonable starter set), `isRecurring` boolean + `recurringIntervalDays` (or a simpler monthly/yearly enum, your call), `occurredAt`/`nextDueAt` as appropriate, `vendor` (free text, e.g. "OVH", "Stripe", "Anthropic"), `notes`, `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, `createdBy` (admin user id). Check how schema changes get applied in this repo (`npx prisma db push`, no `prisma/migrations/` history) and follow it; write the raw SQL to `prisma/manual-migration-*.sql` matching the existing convention from today's other schema changes.

2. **Admin UI** — a new "Accounting" (or "Finance") entry in `lib/admin-groups.ts`, sensibly placed (maybe its own top-level group, or folded into the existing `revenue` group alongside Billing/Catalog/Promotions — use your judgment on IA, but a dedicated top-level "Accounting" group is probably clearer given this is meant to be a real, distinct business function). Build:
   - An expense list/CRUD (add/edit/delete an expense, filter by category/date range) — a `lib/actions-accounting.ts` (or similar) server-actions file following the existing `lib/actions-*.ts` conventions in this codebase (check e.g. `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts` for the pattern: `"use server"`, admin auth-gating, Zod validation, an `audit()` call for the action).
   - A dashboard/overview view: total revenue this month (sum of PAID invoices + relevant wallet activity), total expenses this month (manual entries + the auto-pulled OVH IP cost), a simple net figure. A trailing few months' trend if it's easy to do cleanly (a simple table or small chart), but don't over-engineer visualization for v1 — clarity over cleverness.
   - Recurring-expense handling: since this is a foundational v1, a simple "mark as recurring, shows up in a projected-next-N-months view" is enough — you do not need to build a full auto-generating recurring-expense worker sweep unless it's genuinely trivial to add cleanly; note it as a natural v2 if you skip it.

3. Real data only — no fabricated example expenses. It's fine (expected) for the expense list to start empty; the owner will populate it from here. Do NOT invent a "Anthropic API cost of $X/mo" or similar without a real number — only surface costs you can compute from real data in this system (the OVH IP cost) or leave a clear, empty "add your first expense" state.

## Ground rules

- `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-accounting -b feature/accounting`, symlink `.env`, but give the worktree its OWN real `node_modules` via `npm ci` (not a symlink) before running `npx prisma generate` or touching the schema — a symlinked `node_modules` caused a real production incident earlier today when a schema change leaked into prod's generated Prisma client. This is a hard requirement.
- `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass clean. Add test coverage for any pure calculation logic (e.g. the revenue/expense aggregation math) if it's cleanly separable, following this repo's `npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts` convention.
- This is a new feature with a schema change — moderate scope, not tiny. Commit your work but do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging or production, do NOT run `prisma db push` against any live database. Stop after committing and report back for review.
- If Playwright is available and you can get an authenticated admin session (check other agents' work today for precedent on how), screenshot the new Accounting section. Otherwise clean build + code review is the fallback — say clearly which you did.

Report back: the schema you designed (and why), what the admin UI actually looks like/does, the commit hash, what real data got wired in automatically vs. what's left for manual entry, and what a sensible v2 would add next (e.g. auto-generating recurring expenses, pulling real Stripe fee data, per-customer profitability).

--- CLAUDE.md ---
# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

## Accounting — expense tracking + revenue/cost dashboard (2026-08-26)

Foundational v1 of real business accounting in the admin portal: expense tracking plus a
revenue/expense/net view built on data the platform already has, not a re-entry of revenue and not a
general-ledger system. Built on `feature/accounting`, not merged/deployed — see the branch's PR for
review notes.

**Why now.** The admin portal already tracks customer-facing billing (`Invoice`, `WalletTransaction`,
`User.balanceCents`) but had nowhere to record what the business actually SPENDS, and no single place
showing revenue against cost. This adds that, without duplicating the revenue data that already exists.

**Schema (additive, `prisma/schema.prisma`; raw SQL in `prisma/manual-migration-accounting.sql`).**

- `Expense` — one manually-entered cost line: `description`, `amountCents`, `category` (plain TEXT, not
  a native Postgres enum — see the model's doc-comment for why; the fixed set lives in
  `lib/accounting.ts` `EXPENSE_CATEGORIES`: `INFRASTRUCTURE` / `SOFTWARE` / `PAYMENT_PROCESSING` /
  `MARKETING` / `LEGAL` / `PAYROLL` / `OTHER`), `vendor` (free text), `notes`, `occurredAt`,
  `isRecurring` + `recurringInterval` (`MONTHLY` / `YEARLY`, TEXT for the same reason), `nextDueAt`,
  `createdById` (`User`, `onDelete: SetNull`), timestamps. Indexed on `category`, `occurredAt`, and
  `[isRecurring, nextDueAt]`.
- `User.expensesCreated` — back-relation only, no new column on `User`.

**Pure logic (`lib/accounting.ts`, no DB/IO — unit tested in `test/accounting-calc.test.ts`, 15 tests).**
Month-key bucketing (`monthKey`, `trailingMonthKeys`), per-month sums (`expensesInMonth`,
`totalCents`, `totalsByCategory`), a `buildTrend` helper that pairs a revenue-by-month map against an
expenses-by-month map into a net series, and `projectRecurring` — projects `isRecurring` expenses
forward N calendar months (MONTHLY repeats every month; YEARLY lands only in its anchor month). This
module deliberately does not create/roll forward `Expense` rows — see "Not built" below.

**Auto-pulled cost data (no manual entry required).** The OVH dedicated-IP pool's real monthly cost was
already computed on `/admin/ips` (`OVH_IP_UNIT_COST_CENTS` × pool size, previously a page-local
constant) — promoted to `lib/dedicated-ip.ts` as `OVH_IP_UNIT_COST_CENTS` +
`dedicatedIpPoolMonthlyCostCents()` so both `/admin/ips` and the Accounting dashboard read the exact
same number. It is merged into the dashboard's "Expenses this month" and category breakdown as a live
INFRASTRUCTURE line — it is never written as an `Expense` row, so it can't be edited/deleted from the
Expenses page (that page says so explicitly). No other already-known recurring platform cost (e.g. the
OVH server rental itself) was found in `lib/settings.ts`/`Setting` — there is no such row to pull in, so
the dashboard leaves a labeled empty state inviting a manual entry instead of guessing a number.

**Revenue.** Deliberately reuses the platform's existing `REVENUE_WHERE` wallet-ledger definition
(`lib/admin-metrics.ts`, already the source of truth on `/admin/billing` and `/admin/analytics`) as the
headline "Revenue" figure — earned income only, excluding refunds/affiliate payouts/admin balance
corrections. PAID invoices for the month are shown as a separate "Invoiced (paid)" cross-reference stat
rather than added to wallet revenue, because most orders/renewals write BOTH a wallet debit and an
Invoice row for the same sale — summing both would double-count it.

**Admin UI.**

- `/admin/accounting` — dashboard: this-month revenue / expenses (manual + auto) / net / invoiced-paid
  stat cards, a trailing-6-month revenue-vs-expenses area chart + net table, this-month expense-by-category
  breakdown (including the auto OVH line), and a next-3-months projected-recurring-expenses table. Shows
  a "v1 — foundational" empty-state note when there are no expenses yet.
- `/admin/accounting/expenses` — expense list/CRUD: add form (description, amount, category, vendor,
  date, notes, recurring toggle + interval + next-due), inline edit-in-place per row, delete (confirm),
  category filter chips, and a from/to date-range filter.
- Nav: new top-level **Accounting** group in `lib/admin-groups.ts` (its own group, not folded into
  Revenue — Revenue is customer-facing billing, Accounting is what the platform spends), one entry with
  Overview/Expenses tabs.
- RBAC: new `Area = "accounting"`, **ADMIN-only** (`lib/rbac.ts` `AREA_ROLES`/`HREF_AREA`) — stricter than
  `billing` (which BILLING-role staff also reach) because this surfaces real cost/margin data.

**Server actions (`lib/actions-accounting.ts`, `"use server"`).** `createExpense` / `updateExpense` /
`deleteExpense`, every export `requireArea("accounting")`-gated with a Zod schema and an `AuditLog` row
(`admin.expense_create` / `_update` / `_delete`), matching the `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts` convention.
Added to `test/admin-actions-guards.test.ts`'s `ADMIN_ACTION_FILES` so the structural
authentication/authorization guard tests cover it going forward.

**Not built (intentional v1 scope, noted as v2).**

- No auto-generating recurring-expense worker sweep — a recurring `Expense` is projected forward for
  display (`projectRecurring`) but does not create the next period's row or roll `nextDueAt` forward on
  its own. A clean v2 addition once the projection model has been used for a while.
- No live Stripe processing-fee ingestion — `lib/stripe.ts` is the real payment processor and its fees
  are real costs, but pulling live fee data is more than v1 needs; noted as a future data source.
- No per-customer profitability (revenue minus allocated cost per customer).
- No fabricated example expenses — the table starts empty; every dashboard figure is either real wallet/
  invoice data, a real auto-pulled cost, or a plain "add your first expense" prompt.

## Report

**Schema** — one new model, `Expense` (`prisma/schema.prisma` + `prisma/manual-migration-accounting.sql`): `description`, `amountCents`, `category` and `recurringInterval` (plain `TEXT`, not native Postgres enums — matches this repo's recent convention for `db push`-only additive fields, e.g. `DeployFunnelEvent.type`/`AdsConversion.status`; the fixed value sets live in `lib/accounting.ts`), `vendor`, `notes`, `occurredAt`, `isRecurring`, `nextDueAt`, `createdById` → `User` (`onDelete: SetNull`), timestamps. Indexed on `category`, `occurredAt`, `[isRecurring, nextDueAt]`. Added `User.expensesCreated` back-relation only (no new column on `User`).

**Admin UI** — new top-level **Accounting** nav group (`lib/admin-groups.ts`), gated by a new **ADMIN-only** `accounting` RBAC area (`lib/rbac.ts`, stricter than `billing` since it's real cost/margin data):
- `/admin/accounting` — dashboard: this-month revenue/expenses/net/invoiced-paid stat cards, a trailing-6-month revenue-vs-expense chart + net table, category breakdown, and a 3-month recurring-expense projection. Shows a clear "v1 — foundational, add your first expense" empty state when the table is empty (it starts empty by design).
- `/admin/accounting/expenses` — add/edit/delete CRUD, category filter chips, date-range filter.
- `lib/actions-accounting.ts` (`createExpense`/`updateExpense`/`deleteExpense`) — `requireArea("accounting")`-gated, Zod-validated, `AuditLog`-writing, added to `test/admin-actions-guards.test.ts`'s structural guard list.

**Real data wired in automatically:** revenue reuses the platform's existing `REVENUE_WHERE` wallet-ledger definition (`lib/admin-metrics.ts`, already authoritative on `/admin/billing`/`/admin/analytics`) rather than re-deriving it — PAID invoices are shown as a separate "cross-reference only" stat instead of being added, since summing both would double-count the same sale. The OVH dedicated-IP pool cost (previously a hardcoded `239` cents/IP constant local to `app/admin/ips/page.tsx`) was promoted to a shared `OVH_IP_UNIT_COST_CENTS` + `dedicatedIpPoolMonthlyCostCents()` in `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`, so both the IP page and the new dashboard read the same live number. No OVH-server-rental or other base-infra `Setting` existed to pull in, so that's left as a clearly-labeled manual entry rather than a guess. **Left for manual entry:** everything else (software subscriptions, marketing spend, legal, payroll, etc.) — no fabricated example rows were added.

**Testing:** `lib/accounting.ts` holds all pure aggregation/projection math (month bucketing, category totals, trend building, recurring-expense projection), covered by 13 unit tests in `test/accounting-calc.test.ts` (`npx tsx --test`, all pass). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm run build` clean, including the two new routes. Full test suite shows no new failures — the 32-33 failing tests present are pre-existing on `main` (VPS pricing/promo/checkout tests, verified by running the same suite on pristine main).

Per the task's stated fallback, verification is clean build + `tsc` + tests + manual code review only — no live screenshot.
